buttonLabel: "Explore adventures in Bolivia, Brazil and Chile"
lead: >-
  These routes connect the humid Iguazu Falls, the Atacama Desert, Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat. Compare the off-road sections, changing climates, altitude, seasonal restrictions and differences between available itineraries.
---

## What adventures connect Brazil, Chile and Bolivia?

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The three selected countries are part of **longer itineraries**: travellers also visit Argentina and Peru and, on some journeys, Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia. This is an important distinction from an imagined short trip covering only Brazil, Chile and Bolivia. Between the Brazilian and Chilean sections lies an Argentine stage that includes Buenos Aires.

The shared journey crosses three very different natural regions: tropical forest around Iguazu, the dry Atacama and Bolivia's Altiplano. The main expedition experience in the existing programmes is **travelling by four-wheel drive through high-altitude lagoons and across the salt flat**, rather than a required mountain ascent or multi-day trek.

## Brazil: waterfalls and sightseeing walks

The first days of the [18-day, five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) are spent in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), visiting Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the old city. This is an urban sightseeing section with views of the Atlantic.

The next stop is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Walkways above the gorges offer broad views of the waterfalls. Some programmes allow travellers to add the Macuco Safari boat ride, but on the specified 18-day tour it **costs extra**. A boat excursion cannot be promised to everyone merely because the trip is classified as adventurous.

The journey continues to the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and then via [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) to Chile. Border crossings and internal flights must be considered when calculating the overall duration: travel days leave less time for nature excursions.

## Chile: Santiago and the gateway to Atacama

After [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the route heads towards [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The contrast with Brazil is immediately visible: arid valleys, volcanic massifs and sparse vegetation. On the existing multi-day journeys, this region provides preparation for the onward trip into Bolivia.

When choosing an itinerary, check where the overnight stay takes place and exactly which excursions are included. Stargazing and additional desert outings may be offered separately. Simply stopping in Atacama does not establish that all these activities are part of the tour.

Mornings at altitude can be cold, while daytime demands sun protection and water. A well-organised route takes account of the hours spent on unpaved roads and gradually changing elevation. If you want more time in Chile, compare our [adventure tours in Chile](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/).

## Bolivia: a 4×4 journey past lagoons to Uyuni

The most expedition-like section starts **after crossing the border from Chile into Bolivia**. The [18-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) includes Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, Sol de Mañana geysers, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Travel is by off-road vehicles, with overnight stays at high altitude.

These days require a different pace from a capital-city sightseeing tour. Roads may be unpaved, and weather and access to specific areas depend on conditions. The salt flat and surrounding lagoons are separate stops, not one quick photo opportunity. Flamingos inhabit the areas around some lagoons, but sightings of particular birds cannot be guaranteed.

It is important to discuss personal tolerance of altitude and long drives. Experience with outdoor activities can help, but **these itineraries do not involve a formal mountaineering ascent**. For a more in-depth visit to the Bolivian plateau, compare our [adventure tours in Bolivia](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/).

## Seasons, clothing and the order of countries

| Stage | What to prepare for |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Humidity, waterproof outerwear |
| Atacama | Sun, dry air, cold mornings |
| Bolivian Altiplano | Altitude, warm layers, long drives |

Average temperatures cannot determine one suitable set of clothes for all three regions. Planning needs to consider dates and altitude at every stop, plus road conditions around the lagoons and salt flat. Particular attention is needed for transfers between Atacama and Bolivia and possible weather-related contingency time.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the route, flights, ground transport and accommodation along the actual itinerary. Visas, border crossings, health considerations and access restrictions at natural sites must be assessed for the particular dates, nationalities and participants; a thematic selection cannot replace those checks.

## Tours worth comparing

For an extensive but relatively compact continental journey, consider [five countries in 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). The [six-country, 20-day journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds Uruguay. The [32-day route through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) extends to Ecuador and Colombia.

Event-based versions follow much of the same corridor: the [five-country New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) and the [Champions' Parade itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) depend on dates in Rio. The [private five-country Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) should be compared by its actual activities and Carnival evening, not solely its name. The event affects the timetable for the entire journey, including the high-altitude stage.

To see all itineraries regardless of theme, open the [Bolivia – Brazil – Chile selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile/); to choose by activity, explore [adventure travel](/interests/adventure/).

## Frequently asked questions about adventure travel in Bolivia, Brazil and Chile

### Do I need mountaineering experience?

Usually not. The main active section in these itineraries is travel through the highlands by four-wheel drive. However, altitude and road conditions can affect physical wellbeing, so individual limitations should be considered in advance.

### Is the boat ride at Iguazu Falls included?

Not on every itinerary. The [18-day, five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) offers Macuco Safari for an additional charge.

### Why are Argentina and Peru included in this selection?

They are main countries on the same longer journeys. The catalogue shows itineraries that cover Bolivia, Brazil and Chile even when they also include Argentine and Peruvian stages. Those stages cannot be removed from an existing tour without changing the entire programme.

### Can I shorten the route and visit only the salt flat?

That would be a separate custom itinerary. On the ready-made tours, Uyuni is connected to Atacama, the lagoons and the onward journey to Peru.

kind: multi_country_interest

buttonLabel: "Explore the culture of Bolivia, Brazil and Chile"
lead: >-
  Rio de Janeiro, Santiago's historic centre and ancient Tiwanaku reveal three entirely different periods in South American history. On the existing itineraries, these stops are combined with Argentina and Peru. Compare the cultural programmes in each country, the time allocated to excursions and the places worth spending longer in.
---

## Culture in Brazil, Chile and Bolivia: what is actually included

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These journeys let you experience Rio's Portuguese heritage, Santiago's historical architecture and the Tiwanaku archaeological complex in Bolivia in a single extended trip. However, the existing itineraries cover **five, six or eight countries**: Argentina lies between the Brazilian and Chilean sections, while the route continues to Peru after Bolivia. Thus, the selected three-country combination describes the shared geography of suitable tours, not an independent short trip limited to these countries.

The cultural experiences themselves are very different. Rio is about urban spaces, art and historical buildings; Chile about a capital centre with monuments to civic and national history; Bolivia about the traces of a separate civilisation that flourished long before the Inca state. The Uyuni Salt Flat and high-altitude lagoons, also included in the journey, belong primarily to its nature-focused sections.

## Brazil: Rio beyond the beaches

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itineraries introduce Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and the historic centre. From the elevated viewpoints, the city's relationship with its bay, forested hills and coastline is particularly clear. That landscape has itself become part of Rio's cultural history, shaping public spaces and the patterns of city life.

On the [18-day group journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), the opening days are devoted to Rio, including a tour of its older central districts. This allows visitors to compare colonial architecture with the modern city before travelling to the natural attraction of [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The waterfalls themselves are a natural landmark; visiting them is not a substitute for a cultural tour of Rio.

On trips including the [Carnival Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/), this stage gains a separate event featuring samba and the samba-school procession. The event depends on the dates and itinerary of that specific tour. Standard sightseeing in Rio does not imply Carnival attendance.

## Chile: Santiago's history in its public squares

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the main stops on extended itineraries relate to the historic centre. [Five Latin American Countries in 18 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) includes sightseeing at La Moneda Palace and Plaza de Armas, home to monuments associated with early urban development and state history. The itinerary also introduces today's capital and its setting at the foot of the Andes.

If urban history is your main interest, compare the length of the Santiago stay and the time allocated to the sightseeing tour. These journeys usually continue with a flight to northern Chile and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The desert stage concentrates on landscapes and the transition to a high-altitude route, so it should not automatically be counted as an additional Chilean history excursion.

Our [catalogue of cultural tours in Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/) lets you compare itineraries if one day in Santiago is not enough.

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku before the Inca period

The most significant cultural stop in Bolivia is [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), an archaeological complex near Lake Titicaca. It was the religious and political centre of the pre-Columbian civilisation of the same name. That civilisation flourished around the fifth to ninth centuries, long before the Inca Empire appeared.

Tiwanaku is known for the stone structures of its ceremonial centre. Its monuments include the Kalasasaya Temple, the Gate of the Sun and the remains of the Akapana Pyramid. They reveal architectural and religious-art traditions different from those at Inca sites in Cusco and Machu Picchu. **Tiwanaku should not be described as an “Inca city”**: it belongs to another historical culture. The site is on UNESCO's World Heritage List.

On the [18-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), Tiwanaku is visited on the day of travel from [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) to Puno in Peru. For travellers primarily interested in archaeology, it is essential to check **the actual time at the site**, not merely the presence of the name on the list of stops. The drive, border crossing and onward travel take up part of the day.

The [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) Salt Flat, colourful lagoons and off-road journeys make Bolivia a particularly rich section of the trip, but these are mainly natural and expedition experiences. A different allocation of days may be necessary for a deeper understanding of regional history.

## What Argentina and Peru add

In the usual sequence, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) lies between Rio and Santiago, offering La Boca, San Telmo and a tango show. This is a distinct Argentine cultural experience and should not be attributed to Brazil or Chile.

After Bolivia, the route travels through the [Puno and Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Historical discovery continues here through monuments of the Inca civilisation. On the Uros islands, travellers learn about the tradition of using totora reeds. These stops are **in Peru**, even though they follow immediately after the Bolivian stage. That distinction matters when comparing what is included in each of the three selected countries.

## Choosing a trip for its cultural experiences

| Itinerary | Cultural focus |
|---|---|
| [Five countries in 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Rio, Santiago, Tiwanaku, Cusco |
| [Five countries in 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | The same long route with a Carnival section |
| [Six countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Uruguay added, more stops |
| [Eight countries in 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Additional countries as far as Ecuador and Colombia |

The [five-country New Year programme](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) and [Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) add an event in Rio. An event-focused option makes sense if the date of the celebration is more important than flexibility in allocating time to cultural excursions.

For a rewarding cultural experience, compare **days at historic sites** rather than country counts in the title. Three hours of sightseeing in Santiago, a proper walk through Rio and a Tiwanaku visit during a border-transfer day provide different depths of insight. If Bolivian archaeology or Chilean museums matter more to you than other experiences, Ada Tours can discuss a different schedule and a custom route. This new proposal should be distinguished from an existing multi-day programme.

All relevant journeys are listed under [Bolivia – Brazil – Chile](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile/), with related cultural destinations in our [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural tours in Brazil, Chile and Bolivia

### Is Tiwanaku an Inca site?

No. Tiwanaku belongs to a separate pre-Columbian civilisation that flourished before the Inca Empire. The same extended journey includes Inca monuments later in Peru, around Cusco and Machu Picchu.

### Is there enough time for Tiwanaku on every tour?

The stop is listed in existing extended itineraries, but on some trips it falls on a travel day between Bolivia and Peru. Check the actual visiting time against your dates, border arrangements and transport.

### Where does Carnival take place on the route?

The Champions' Parade is held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, when it forms part of a particular event-focused itinerary. Sightseeing in Santiago and visiting Tiwanaku are not themselves related to Carnival.

### Why are tours through five or more countries listed here?

This selection contains journeys with Bolivia, Brazil and Chile in their main itinerary and a substantial focus on culture and history. Argentina, Peru and other countries remain parts of those same existing tours; they cannot automatically be removed by selecting the filter.

targetPath: /multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile/interests/events-and-festivals/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore festive journeys through Bolivia, Brazil and Chile"
lead: >-
  Event-focused journeys through Bolivia, Brazil and Chile begin with Carnival or New Year in Rio de Janeiro. They then travel through Argentina and Chile's Atacama to Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni. In these particular itineraries, Chile and Bolivia provide nature experiences, not local festivals. The central planning challenge is to reconcile the fixed event dates with the onward journey into the Andes.
---

## A Brazilian celebration followed by the highlands of Chile and Bolivia

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} connecting [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) under the Events and Festivals theme. **The main event takes place in Rio de Janeiro**: New Year's Eve on Copacabana or Carnival attendance, including a separate version with the Champions' Parade. The other countries are included for their cities, mountains and deserts. None of these three itineraries promises a separate festival in Chile or Bolivia.

All matching trips cover **five main countries**. In addition to the selected three, they visit Argentina and Peru. This selection should not be mistaken for a short “Rio – Santiago – Uyuni” tour: the journey also includes Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires, drives across the Altiplano and a final section in Peru. Removing these would mean designing a different itinerary.

See the [Bolivia – Brazil – Chile selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile/) to compare the full geography. Here we explain how a fixed celebration date determines the timing of the high-altitude sections.

## Three celebrations and three different itineraries

| Programme | Event focus |
|---|---|
| [New Year and five countries, 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) | December 31 on Copacabana |
| [Carnival tour, 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Attending Carnival at the Sambadrome |
| [Five countries with the Champions' Parade, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | The separate Champions' Parade |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_na_16_dnej_na_novyj_god,tour_source_karnaval_5_stran,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala}}

The [New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) begins with arrival in Rio on December 30; the night of December 31 to January 1 is devoted to Copacabana. Sightseeing in Rio and travel to Iguazu follow.

Carnival journeys are scheduled around the samba-school processions, but **the main Carnival parades and the Champions' Parade are separate events on different dates**. LIESA's official 2027 calendar lists the principal parades for February 7–9 and the Champions' Parade for February 13. These dates are useful for selecting an event but do not, by themselves, confirm a specific Ada Tours departure, availability or ticket category. The chosen tour offer determines the actual inclusions and booking terms.

## Brazil: why the journey starts in Rio

[Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) is the emotional centre of these itineraries. The New Year version features a celebratory evening beside the ocean; Carnival versions include spectator seating and samba-school parades. City excursions to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain accompany this portion.

The route then continues to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and the Argentine side of the falls. Travelling from Rio to Chile is therefore not a direct flight to the desert: tourists visit Buenos Aires before Santiago. This affects the number of overnight stays and ticket combinations.

If your main aim is simply to enjoy festive days in Brazil, the rest of a five-country tour may feel too intensive. [Festival journeys across several countries](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/) offer opportunities to compare more focused alternatives.

## Chile: Santiago and the transition to Atacama

In Chile, the journey begins in Santiago, then includes a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). **This is a move from a tropical city celebration to the desert and high altitude**, not another day at a festival.

In San Pedro, it is important to assess how you feel and prepare for the onward journey. The next section follows off-road tracks into Bolivia through high-altitude areas with lagoons, volcanoes and hot springs. For someone arriving from humid Rio, the altitude and dry air will feel quite different. Agree on the pace, suitable clothing and enough rest time in advance.

Do not assume the Atacama weather will be the same on New Year and Carnival itineraries. The event chosen in Rio shifts the calendar for the rest of the journey. Daylight hours, road conditions and the feasibility of particular excursions need checking for the specific dates.

## Bolivia: jeeps, lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat

Some of the most striking nature days take place on the Bolivian Altiplano. Tourists cross from Chile and travel by 4×4 vehicles through high-altitude lagoons. Listed sights include Licancabur Volcano, colourful lagoons, geysers and hot springs, followed by [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

This is a substantial multi-day section. Roads cross the highlands, not an urban expressway. Warm windproof clothes, sun protection and a discussion of personal tolerance for altitude are necessary. These climbs and drives should not be described as an effortless excursion immediately after a beach celebration.

Between December and February, conditions on and around the salt flat depend on rainfall. A wet surface can sometimes produce reflections, but vehicle routes and road conditions are determined by safety. Neither the mirror effect nor access to every stop can be guaranteed from the travel month alone.

After Uyuni, the programmes head to La Paz and then Lake Titicaca and Peru. This means the timing of the Bolivia stage is closely linked with the dates of the final Peruvian excursions, even for those most interested in Bolivia itself.

## The hardest part of combining these experiences

The central compromise is **a fixed festival date versus flexibility in a high-altitude itinerary**. New Year or the Champions' Parade cannot simply be moved by a week, while weather in Atacama and Bolivia, intercity flights and border procedures all call for contingency time.

The full country list also matters: Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Entry documents, possible re-entries, transit and insurance requirements must be checked for each nationality. Inclusions need separate agreement too, particularly event tickets and domestic flights.

Ada Tours helps choose the event, connect it with a workable itinerary and coordinate transfers and accommodation. But exact weather conditions, event-ticket availability and border crossings at fixed times cannot be promised.

## Frequently asked questions about festive travel through Bolivia, Brazil and Chile

### Do these programmes include festivals in Bolivia and Chile?

The confirmed scheduled event takes place in Rio de Janeiro. Chile and Bolivia feature city sightseeing, Atacama and high-altitude nature excursions.

### Can I attend Carnival and then go straight to Uyuni?

The existing itinerary includes Iguazu, Buenos Aires and the Chilean section in between. A direct, shortened route would require new calculations and agreements, not merely a different transfer.

### Does Uyuni look the same in January and February?

No. Conditions depend on actual rainfall and the state of the salt flat. Water reflections and access to specific areas cannot be guaranteed by the date alone.

### Should altitude be considered after relaxing in Rio?

Yes. The lowland, tropical opening is followed by the highlands of Chile and Bolivia. Discuss the trip's pace and personal tolerance of altitude before booking.

The rest of the programme focuses on Rio, Iguazu, Atacama and the Bolivian highlands. This is best viewed as a sightseeing journey with an optional wine experience."

## Bolivia, Brazil and Chile: where food and wine fit into the route

For travellers choosing South America for its food and wine, it is important to distinguish **an organised tasting experience** from ordinary meal stops. Our Bolivia–Brazil–Chile selection includes a [20-day journey through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). Its Chilean section offers a wine excursion in the Maipo Valley. In Brazil and Bolivia, the itinerary focuses primarily on cities, natural landmarks and the highlands.

On this tour, food and wine remain **a secondary interest**, not the main purpose of the trip. That distinction is significant: appearing in a themed catalogue does not mean tastings or cooking activities are offered in all three countries. Assess the confirmed inclusions first, then decide whether enough time is devoted to food and wine.

## Chile: Maipo Valley wineries as a separate extra

The main location for wine experiences is the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) near [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The day in the capital includes a city tour, while a separate [Maipo winery excursion with tasting](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) is offered as an option.

The excursion costs **$230 per person, with a minimum of 2 participants**. This is an optional service: it is not included merely because the tour appears in the gastronomy catalogue. Time must be coordinated with the Santiago sightseeing tour, and the winery visit must be confirmed.

Maipo is an appealing choice for those who want to taste Chilean wine in its place of production. Unlike a tasting over dinner, a winery visit also introduces the wine-growing region. The particular wineries, wines served and tasting arrangements depend on the confirmed excursion, so it would be misleading to promise a specific brand or number of samples in advance.

## Brazil: Rio and Iguazu without a dedicated food tour

The Brazil section covers [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and Iguazu Falls are the principal attractions. No separate organised cooking workshop, wine tasting or production-site tour is included in this Brazilian portion.

Rio offers opportunities to try local food in free time, but visiting a restaurant independently is different from an included specialist excursion. If cuisine is a priority, consider how much free time remains between sightseeing and the domestic flight to Iguazu.

If you primarily want to explore and enjoy Brazil, compare [tours in Brazil](/brazil/tour/) with [the country's food-and-wine itineraries](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/brazil/). The actual programme determines whether food is an independent part of the route or simply an enjoyable addition to its main attractions.

## Bolivia: a high-altitude expedition, not a gastronomy section

After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the route crosses into Bolivia and continues by 4×4. Stops include Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, Sol de Mañana geysers, Laguna Colorada and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The journey then continues via [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and Tiwanaku into Peru.

Here, food is primarily a practical part of managing long drives. The two-day high-altitude section calls for suitable meal arrangements and enough drinking water. Specialist tastings of Bolivian cuisine and winery visits are not included in this itinerary.

Parts of the route reach considerable elevations, including [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The itinerary allows time to acclimatise in Atacama before crossing the border. Scheduling a late wine tasting and an early departure to the mountains as an obligatory combination, without checking the timetable or how you feel, would be unwise.

## What the complete tour involves

| Country | Role in the journey |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Cities and Iguazu |
| Chile | Santiago and an optional wine excursion |
| Bolivia | Altiplano and Uyuni |

On the actual route, Argentina and Uruguay also follow Brazil. Chile, Bolivia and Peru come later. Therefore, “Bolivia + Brazil + Chile” is part of **a six-country itinerary**, not three consecutive sections that can be automatically joined without additional flights and days.

The tour suits someone whose primary goal is to explore several South American countries while including one wine stop. If you want a series of tastings, multiple wine regions and food-focused experiences almost every day, a different type of itinerary would be more appropriate. Explore [multi-country gastronomy journeys](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) or the full [Food and Wine theme](/interests/food-and-wine/).

The [general Bolivia – Brazil – Chile catalogue](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile/) is useful too: there, the selection is based on geography rather than a particular interest. Compare actual inclusions, duration, transfers and optional activities before choosing.

## Adding a wine tasting without losing a sightseeing day

First, keep track of the time already allocated to Santiago in the main route. Then check the winery excursion's duration, transfer arrangements and whether it can fit alongside the city sightseeing tour. On journeys involving several flights, the additional stop must work with the actual schedule.

Optional activities should be discussed before the itinerary is finalised, especially for two travellers when a tasting has a minimum group size. The base-tour price, airfares, room category and separate excursion conditions must be considered individually. Itineraries that look similar may differ considerably in what they include.

## Frequently asked questions about the gastronomy itinerary

### Is the Chilean wine tasting included in the tour price?

No. The [Maipo Valley excursion](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) costs extra: $230 per person, with at least 2 participants.

### Is there a separate Bolivian gastronomy programme on this tour?

No such section is included in our 20-day route. The Bolivian portion focuses on high-altitude lagoons, salt flats, Uyuni, La Paz and the monuments at Tiwanaku.

### Can I visit only Bolivia, Brazil and Chile without other countries?

This selection presents the three countries as part of an existing six-country journey. A shorter version would require separate agreement on the route and inclusions; the existing tour also travels through Argentina, Uruguay and Peru.

### Who is this option particularly suitable for?

Travellers whose main aim is an extensive South American sightseeing journey and who see the wine tasting as an additional experience during their stay in Santiago.

## Bolivia, Brazil and Chile: from humid forests to a salt desert

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with nature stops along routes through Bolivia, Brazil and Chile. Consider the whole journey from the outset: all existing options also include **Argentina and Peru**, while some add Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia. This is not a direct flight from Brazil to Bolivia for a single day on a salt flat.

The defining feature is the dramatic change in conditions. In Brazil, travellers see the green slopes of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and the humid Iguazu forest. In Chile, after Santiago they fly to Calama and continue to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Bolivia brings high-altitude roads and lakes. Different clothing, allowances for travel time and paces of rest are needed.

## What Brazil's natural attractions actually offer

[Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) greets travellers with the ocean, bays and rocky peaks. Itineraries include Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer as well as Sugarloaf Mountain; the nature views here are seen from urban viewpoints. These should not be presented as a separate hike through wilderness forest.

Next is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Sightseeing paths run beside numerous cascades amid the Atlantic Forest. According to UNESCO, the natural complex comprises adjoining protected parks in Brazil and Argentina. That is why most tours continue to [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), which has different observation walkways. Options such as [Parque das Aves](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and a boat ride may cost extra: mentioning them in a regional description does not mean they are included in your chosen fare.

The Brazilian stage is particularly good for discovering what humid subtropical landscapes look like. Chile and Bolivia offer almost the opposite experience: dry expanses, mineral-rich lagoons, volcanic landforms and cold nights.

## Chile: the crucial transition to Atacama and altitude

After the Argentine stage, itineraries continue to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The capital mainly features a city sightseeing tour. Travellers then fly to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). On some itineraries, this day is expressly described as acclimatisation time before Bolivia.

A full excursion to every Atacama valley should not be attributed to every tour. What is confirmed here is exposure to the high-altitude desert environment, a change of climate and preparation for the onward journey. A telescope-based stargazing excursion is offered **as an option** in some descriptions; it is not a required nature activity.

This is where travellers begin to notice the greatest change in how they feel. After coastal and city stops, the air becomes drier, nights colder and the road to Bolivia climbs still higher. Continuing without regard for altitude simply because the preceding days felt easy would be risky.

## Bolivia: a two-day sequence worth preserving

From San Pedro, the route leads to the Bolivian border, where the 4×4 road journey begins. The first nature day includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) beside a volcanic massif, the rocky Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Flamingos are mentioned in the itineraries: these lagoons are a natural habitat for the birds, but sightings of every group at any particular time are not guaranteed.

The following stage takes travellers past high-altitude lagoons, volcanoes and salt flats towards [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The surface may display dry salt patterns or reflections in standing water. Conditions determine access to particular sites and the passability of the tracks. The itineraries include stops at salt-production locations and Incahuasi Island; travelling across the plateau occupies the longest part of the day.

Reducing the Bolivia section to one attractive photograph against a salt-flat backdrop would make little sense if you want to see its varied natural landscapes. Lagoons, geothermal fields and the salt flat occupy different stretches of the road. Customising the itinerary requires consideration of actual jeep travel speeds, road conditions, the border crossing and overnight accommodation in remote areas.

## Seasons and health: a compromise among three climates

The journey combines heat and humidity at Iguazu, the drier Atacama and cold high-altitude nights in Bolivia. There is no single “best week” for all nature sections. Uyuni looks particularly different when water covers its surface, but wet conditions can also restrict off-road routes. Start by deciding your main priority when choosing dates: the waterfalls, access roads to lagoons or the possibility of sky reflections on the salt flat.

The CDC recommends gaining altitude gradually where possible. Before ascending to the Altiplano, assess your tolerance of height, discuss individual medical contraindications with a doctor, check insurance terms and allow time for rest. Pack protection from sun, wind and cold, plus clothing suitable for humid weather during the Brazil section. Ada Tours helps coordinate transport connections, highland overnight stops and the time devoted to nature excursions on a particular itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia, Brazil and Chile

### Are the Argentine waterfalls included even though three other countries appear in the heading?

Yes. Existing tours in this selection include both sides of Iguazu Falls. Argentina is part of the full main route even though it is not named in the selected combination.

### Can all the Bolivian lagoons be seen in one day?

The programmes allocate consecutive jeep-travel days to the highlands and salt flat. A shorter plan must be assessed against distances, weather and overnight arrangements, not on the assumption that all the sites are near one another.

### Is the Atacama stargazing excursion compulsory?

No. Some tours offer a nighttime telescope excursion as an extra. Its availability and terms should be checked against the chosen programme.
